examples.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Function With an Irreducible Binomial Quadratic Factor
examples.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor $x^2+4$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{({x}^{2}+4)}+\frac{C}{(x-1)}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x^2+4)(x-1),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+3 & =(Ax+B)(x-1)+C({x}^{2}+4)\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=-1, B=1,$ and $C=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\dfrac{2x+3}{(x^2+4)(x-1)} = \dfrac{-x+1}{x^2+4} +\dfrac{1}{x-1}.
$$

Now we integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{-x+1}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{1}{x-1})\text{d}x \\  & =-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u = x^2+4.$ Then $2x\,\textrm{d}x=\textrm{d}u,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+4| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral,  we use the fact that $\displaystyle \int \dfrac{1}{x^2+a^2} \, \textrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{a}\arctan\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{x-1}\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|.\end{aligned}
$$

So we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4)+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|+K\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}=\frac{2x+B}{{x}^{2}+5}-\frac{1}{x+1},
$$

where $B$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}\,\text{d}x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $B.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+5x-2 & =(2x+B)(x+1)-({x}^{2}+5).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=0$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{0}^{2}+5(0)-2 & =(2(0)+B)(0+1)-({0}^{2}+5) \\ -2 & =B-5 \\ B & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x+3}{{x}^{2}+5}-\frac{1}{x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+5}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{3}{{x}^{2}+5}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution ${x}^{2}+5=u.$ Then, $2x\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+5}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+5).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+5}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+(\sqrt{5})^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{5}}) \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{5}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}x}{5}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+1}\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+5)+\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{5}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}x}{5})-\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+C\end{aligned}
$$
